Decode Autoregressive LLM 不是一次生成整段答案，而是反复预测下一个 Token。在线推理要把 Prefill 与 Decode 分开看：前者处理输入前缀并建立上下文状态，后者逐 Token 生成并复用已有 KV。 FIG.1.1 · INFERENCE LIFECYCLE 从文本到下一个 Token 1 · TOKENIZE Text → Token IDs 使用目标模型对应 tokenizer；Token 数决定上下文、成本与缓存身份。 2 · PREFILL Input tokens → hidden state 输入批量处理，通常主导 TTFT 中的模型前缀计算。 3 · LOGITS Vocabulary scores 输出层为候选 Token 产生 logits。 4 · SAMPLE Temperature / Top-p 采样策略控制变化性，不提供真实性。 5 · DECODE Next token → repeat 逐 Token 生成；输出越长，顺序 Decode 越多。 核心规则 Prefill and Decode are different performance regimes; diagnose them separately. 1.2 Transformer：理解 Q/K/V，而不是把 Attention 当数据库 Transformer 通过多层 Attention 与前馈变换构造上下文表征。Attention 的核心是 Q/K 的兼容度打分，再用归一化权重聚合 V；它描述网络内部依赖，不等于事实检索或验证。 Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ) V 架构 信息可见性 典型用途 关键修正 Encoder-only bidirectional classification · embedding · labeling 更偏表征学习 Decoder-only causal open-ended autoregressive generation 主流生成架构之一，不是唯一生成架构 Encoder–Decoder encoder bidirectional + decoder causal translation · summarization · seq2seq 同样可以生成 RoPE 通过位置相关旋转把相对位置信息带入 Attention，但不保证无限长度可靠外推；FlashAttention 通过 IO-aware tiling 避免在 HBM 中物化完整 N×N score matrix，改变的是精确 Attention 的实现效率，而不是语义定义。 1.3 Token 与 Context：字符是 UI 数量，Token 才是 Runtime 数量 Token 可能是单词、子词、字节片段、标点、空格敏感片段或代码片段；具体划分由 tokenizer 决定。因此不能把固定字符数/单词数换算规则当作工程事实。 FIG.1.2 · CONTEXT BUDGET Context Window 是共享预算，不是 RAG 专属容量 INSTRUCTIONS System / Developer 核心约束、角色与任务协议。 CAPABILITIES Tool schemas / examples 工具定义与 few-shot 也占 Token。 EVIDENCE History / Memory / RAG 历史、记忆与检索证据必须竞争同一预算。 RESERVE Output / reasoning 必须为输出和必要的推理预算预留空间。 容量 ≠ 利用率 长 Context 能装下更多 Token，但相关证据是否被可靠利用仍是模型、长度、位置和 Prompt Layout 的经验问题。 当 Prompt + 文档超窗时，优先考虑 rerank、减少 top-k、去重、结构化 state、分解任务、压缩或 staged synthesis。Lost in the Middle 说明相关信息位置在某些长上下文任务中会影响性能，因此应做 position-sensitive eval，而不是机械地把重要内容永远放在两头。 1.4 Sampling：Temperature / Top-p 只控制变化性 机制 控制什么 不解决什么 Temperature 分布 sharpness / randomness 事实缺失、错误检索、权限、业务有效性、工具副作用 Top-p 进入采样候选集的累计概率质量 常见误区 Temperature = 0 ≠ truth. 低温可以降低采样变化，但不能把错误知识、错误 Evidence 或错误 Tool Result 变成正确答案，也不保证跨后端/版本 bit-for-bit 一致。 1.5 Embeddings：Similarity 是候选生成，不是 Correctness Embedding 把文本或对象映射到向量空间。Dot Product 同时受方向与向量 magnitude 影响；Cosine 会归一化 magnitude。若向量已经 L2-normalized，Dot Product 与 Cosine 可以产生相同 ranking——但这是具体 embedding family 的性质，不是所有向量模型的默认定律。 x · y = ||x|| ||y|| cos θ cos(x,y) = (x · y) / (||x|| ||y||) Dense retrieval 容易把主题相近但动作相反、版本不同、日期不同的内容放在一起。因此生产检索通常需要 Authorization / Metadata → Exact/BM25/Dense → Rerank → Evidence Validation。 1.6 Base、Instruct 与 Post-training Base model 主要学习 next-token continuation；Instruct / aligned model 在预训练之后继续做行为适配。Post-training 可能包含 SFT、preference data、reward modeling、RL-based optimization、DPO 或安全训练，不应把 instruct 简化成“等于 RLHF”。 FIG.1.3 · POST-TRAINING PATHS Preference optimization 不是单一路线 CLASSIC RLHF SFT → Reward Model → PPO 奖励模型提供 proxy；策略优化需要防止过度偏离 reference。 DPO Preference pairs → direct objective 在特定 formulation 下直接优化 preference，不单独训练 RM 再跑 PPO。 ORIGINAL GRPO Group samples → relative advantage 原始 DeepSeekMath GRPO 用组内 reward 统计建立相对 advantage，避免单独 critic/value model。 保护指标 Preference win-rate 上升时仍要单独保护 factuality、task success、safety 和 calibration；代理指标变好不等于真实目标全都变好。 1.7 Hallucination：Plausibility 天生存在，Truthfulness 需要工程化 Hallucination 可能来自参数知识缺失/过时、Prompt 不完整、Retrieval 失败、Context 冲突、Tool Result 错误、unsupported inference，或系统本应拒答却强迫模型继续生成。 缓解方式 获得什么 付出什么 Grounding / RAG 外部 Evidence 与可更新事实 检索延迟、索引维护、Context Token、召回失败 Scope + Abstention 不确定时不猜 Coverage 下降与 false refusal Verification / Tool 外部检查或 deterministic evidence 额外延迟、成本和 verifier failure 1.8 Prompt vs RAG vs Fine-tuning：先诊断 Failure Type 问题类型 首选杠杆 为什么 指令 / 风格 / 输出格式 Prompt / Few-shot 最快、最便宜、最容易回滚 缺少动态 / 私有 / 可追溯事实 RAG / Tool / External Context 知识可更新、可授权、可引用 长期重复的行为缺口 Fine-tuning / Adaptation 把稳定行为模式写入模型参数 模型能力上限 更强/更专用模型或架构变化 Prompt 不能制造不存在的能力 记忆法 Prompt for behavior · RAG for changing evidence · Fine-tuning for repeated behavior. LoRA 通过冻结 base weights、训练低秩更新矩阵来降低可训练参数量；QLoRA 把 quantized frozen base 与 LoRA adapters 结合。4-bit weights 不代表总训练内存一定缩小 4 倍，因为 activations、optimizer、adapter 和临时 buffer 仍然存在。 1.9 Structured Output：结构正确不等于任务正确 Prompt-only JSON → JSON mode → strict schema / constrained decoding → semantic validation → permission / risk gate → host execution 当前 OpenAI Structured Outputs 在支持的 API / JSON Schema subset 上可以使用 strict schema 约束结构；JSON Mode 只保证有效 JSON。无论哪一种，都不能把 schema-valid 直接当成 factually correct、business-valid 或 authorized。 三层边界 Syntax validity ≠ semantic validity ≠ authorization. 1.10 Latency 与 Cache：先分解链路 Client / Network → Gateway / Queue → Prompt Assembly / Retrieval → Prefill / TTFT → Decode → Tool / Validation → Final Delivery 高价值优化通常来自：减少输出 Token、在质量允许时用更小/更快模型、减少无效输入、减少串行请求、并行独立步骤、复用缓存。Streaming 主要降低 perceived latency，并不一定降低总计算或 task completion time。 Cache 复用什么 主要边界 Application Cache 数据、结果、组装后的 artifact 业务 invalidation Prompt / Prefix Cache 匹配前缀的 Prefill 工作 Token-level prefix identity / provider policy KV Cache 单次 Decode 中历史 K/V Context length / memory Semantic Cache 语义相似请求的 response / tool result 语义等价与 freshness 1.11 Model Selection 与 Migration Eval 模型选择是多目标工程决策：Task quality、modality、tool/structured-output support、context behavior、latency、throughput、cost、privacy、hosting、version lifecycle 都需要进入 Task Contract。Self-host 也不能只比较 GPU 小时价与 API Token 价，还要计算 utilization、capacity headroom、SRE、安全、升级、可用性和质量差距。 Production baseline → frozen eval set → candidate model replay → per-example + slice diff → tool/schema compatibility → latency + cost → shadow / canary → ship / hold / rollback 发布原则 Model behavior is a versioned dependency; treat migration like a production release. 1.12 FDE 52 题覆盖边界 公开题库的 52 道题横跨整本 Handbook：模型基础归本章；Vector Search 归 Chapter 02/03；Tool Calling 归 Chapter 06；Agent 是否适用归 Chapter 08；Eval 归 Chapter 09；Prompt Injection、Sandbox、Serving 与 KV/Prefix Cache 深入归 Chapter 10。Interview archive 保留逐题答题卡，但 canonical meaning 继续由各章节拥有。 来源边界 公开 GitHub Markdown 只有题目、难度标签、reported-company 标签、短 teaser 和 answer link，并不包含完整专家答案。本章是独立作答 + 一手资料核验，不复制或重构锁定答案；difficulty/company 标签也不当作招聘统计事实。 1.13 Canonical Rules 必须记住 Characters are a UI quantity; tokens are a model-runtime quantity. A long context window is capacity; evidence utilization is empirical. Sampling controls variability; it does not create truth. Semantic similarity is candidate generation, not correctness. Syntax validity is not semantic validity, and semantic validity is not authorization. Capacity, selection, and reuse are separate design axes. ← 目录 02 企业检索基础 →
textEn: CHAPTER 01 Model / API / Context Foundations Model foundations are not a list of parameters. They explain how input becomes tokens, how tokens move through a Transformer, how context is budgeted, how outputs are sampled, when to use RAG, fine-tuning or caching, and how to verify that a model change did not break production behavior. 1. 1 Generation: Prefill and Decode An autoregressive LLM does not generate an entire answer at once. It repeatedly predicts the next token. Online inference should separate Prefill from Decode: Prefill processes the input prefix and establishes context state; Decode generates tokens sequentially while reusing prior KV state. FIG. 1. 1 · INFERENCE LIFECYCLE From text to the next token 1 · TOKENIZE Text → Token IDs Use the target model's tokenizer; token count drives context, cost, and cache identity. 2 · PREFILL Input tokens → hidden state Input tokens are processed together and often dominate model-side prefix work before the first token. 3 · LOGITS Vocabulary scores The output layer produces logits over candidate tokens. 4 · SAMPLE Temperature / Top-p Sampling controls variability; it does not create truth. 5 · DECODE Next token → repeat Generation proceeds token by token; longer outputs require more sequential decode steps. Core rule Prefill and Decode are different performance regimes; diagnose them separately. 1. 2 Transformer: Understand Q/K/V without treating attention as a database A Transformer builds contextual representations through repeated attention and feed-forward transformations. Attention scores Q/K compatibility and uses normalized weights to aggregate V; it models internal dependencies, not factual retrieval or verification. Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ) V Family Visibility Typical use Correction Encoder-only bidirectional classification · embedding · labeling Representation-oriented Decoder-only causal open-ended autoregressive generation A dominant generation architecture, not the only one Encoder–Decoder encoder bidirectional + decoder causal translation · summarization · seq2seq Also supports generation RoPE injects relative-position structure through position-dependent rotations, but it does not guarantee unlimited reliable extrapolation. FlashAttention uses IO-aware tiling to avoid materializing the full N×N score matrix in HBM; it changes the implementation efficiency of exact attention, not its semantic definition. 1. 3 Tokens and Context: characters are a UI quantity; tokens are a runtime quantity A token may be a word, subword, byte fragment, punctuation, whitespace-sensitive fragment, or code fragment; the tokenizer decides. Fixed character-to-token or word-to-token ratios are not engineering facts. FIG. 1. 2 · CONTEXT BUDGET The context window is a shared budget, not RAG-only capacity INSTRUCTIONS System / Developer Core constraints, role and task contract. CAPABILITIES Tool schemas / examples Tool definitions and few-shot examples also consume tokens. EVIDENCE History / Memory / RAG History, memory and retrieved evidence compete for the same budget. RESERVE Output / reasoning Reserve space for output and any required reasoning budget. Capacity ≠ utilization A long context can hold more tokens, but reliable evidence use remains an empirical property of the model, length, evidence position, and prompt layout. When prompts plus documents exceed the window, consider reranking, smaller top-k, deduplication, structured state, task decomposition, compression, or staged synthesis. Lost in the Middle shows that evidence position can affect performance on some long-context tasks, so run position-sensitive evals rather than mechanically placing all important content at the edges. 1. 4 Sampling: Temperature and top-p control variability Mechanism Controls Does not solve Temperature Distribution sharpness / randomness Missing facts, bad retrieval, authorization, business validity, tool side effects Top-p Cumulative probability mass admitted to sampling Common trap Temperature = 0 ≠ truth. Low temperature can reduce sampling variance, but it cannot turn wrong knowledge, evidence, or tool results into truth, nor guarantee bit-for-bit identity across every backend or model version. 1. 5 Embeddings: similarity generates candidates; it does not prove correctness Embeddings map text or items into a vector space. Dot product depends on both direction and magnitude, while cosine normalizes magnitude. If vectors are L2-normalized, dot product and cosine can produce identical rankings—but that is a property of a particular embedding family, not a universal default. x · y = ||x|| ||y|| cos θ cos(x, y) = (x · y) / (||x|| ||y||) Dense retrieval can place topically similar but operationally opposite, differently versioned, or differently dated items together. Production retrieval therefore typically needs Authorization / Metadata → Exact/BM25/Dense → Rerank → Evidence Validation. 1. 6 Base, instruct, and post-training A base model primarily learns next-token continuation. Instruct/aligned models receive additional behavioral adaptation after pretraining. Post-training may include SFT, preference data, reward modeling, RL-based optimization, DPO, or safety training; instruct should not be reduced to 'equals RLHF'. FIG. 1. 3 · POST-TRAINING PATHS Preference optimization is not a single pipeline CLASSIC RLHF SFT → Reward Model → PPO A reward model provides a proxy; policy optimization needs control against excessive drift from the reference. DPO Preference pairs → direct objective Under its formulation, directly optimizes preferences without separately training a reward model and then PPO. ORIGINAL GRPO Group samples → relative advantage Original DeepSeekMath GRPO uses group-relative reward statistics and avoids a separate critic/value model. Protected metrics Even when preference win-rate improves, protect factuality, task success, safety, and calibration separately; a better proxy does not mean every real objective improved. 1. 7 Hallucination: plausibility is native; truthfulness must be engineered Hallucination can come from missing/stale parametric knowledge, underspecified prompts, retrieval failure, contradictory context, bad tool results, unsupported inference, or an application forcing an answer when it should abstain. Mitigation Gain Cost Grounding / RAG External evidence and fresh facts Retrieval latency, index maintenance, context tokens, retrieval failure Scope + Abstention Do not guess under insufficient evidence Lower coverage and false-refusal risk Verification / Tool External check or deterministic evidence Additional latency, cost, and verifier failure modes 1. 8 Prompt vs RAG vs fine-tuning: diagnose the failure type first Failure type First lever Why Instruction / style / output format Prompt / Few-shot Fastest, cheapest, easiest to roll back Missing dynamic/private/provenance-sensitive facts RAG / Tool / External Context Knowledge remains updatable, authorizable, and citable Repeated stable behavioral gap Fine-tuning / Adaptation Move stable behavioral patterns into model parameters Capability ceiling Stronger/specialized model or architecture change Prompting cannot create missing capability Recall Prompt for behavior · RAG for changing evidence · Fine-tuning for repeated behavior. LoRA freezes base weights and trains low-rank update matrices to reduce trainable parameters. QLoRA combines a quantized frozen base with LoRA adapters. Four-bit weights do not imply total training memory is exactly four times smaller because activations, optimizer state, adapters, and temporary buffers still exist. 1. 9 Structured Output: correct shape does not mean correct task semantics Prompt-only JSON → JSON mode → strict schema / constrained decoding → semantic validation → permission / risk gate → host execution Current OpenAI Structured Outputs can enforce a strict schema on supported APIs and JSON Schema subsets; JSON Mode guarantees valid JSON only. Neither allows schema-valid output to be treated as automatically factually correct, business-valid, or authorized. Three boundaries Syntax validity ≠ semantic validity ≠ authorization. 1. 10 Latency and caching: decompose the path first Client / Network → Gateway / Queue → Prompt Assembly / Retrieval → Prefill / TTFT → Decode → Tool / Validation → Final Delivery High-value latency improvements usually come from fewer output tokens, smaller/faster models where quality allows, less useless input, fewer sequential requests, parallel independent work, and caching. Streaming mainly improves perceived latency; it does not necessarily reduce total compute or task completion time. Cache What it reuses Main boundary Application Cache Data, results, assembled artifacts Business invalidation Prompt / Prefix Cache Prefill work for matching prefixes Token-level prefix identity / provider policy KV Cache Past K/V within a generation Context length / memory Semantic Cache Responses/tool results for semantically similar requests Semantic equivalence and freshness 1. 11 Model Selection and migration evaluation Model selection is a multi-objective engineering decision. Task quality, modality, tool/structured-output support, context behavior, latency, throughput, cost, privacy, hosting, and version lifecycle all belong in the task contract. Self-hosting cannot be decided by comparing GPU hourly price with API token price alone; utilization, capacity headroom, SRE, security, upgrades, availability, and quality gap all matter. Production baseline → frozen eval set → candidate model replay → per-example + slice diff → tool/schema compatibility → latency + cost → shadow / canary → ship / hold / rollback Release principle Model behavior is a versioned dependency; treat migration like a production release. 1. 12 FDE 52-question coverage boundary The 52 public interview prompts span the entire Handbook: model fundamentals belong here; vector search belongs to Chapters 02/03; tool calling to Chapter 06; whether to use an agent to Chapter 08; evaluation to Chapter 09; and prompt injection, sandboxing, serving, and deep KV/prefix-cache topics to Chapter 10. The interview archive keeps a per-question answer map while canonical meaning remains with the owning chapters. Source boundary The public GitHub Markdown contains prompts, difficulty labels, reported-company labels, short teasers, and answer links—not the full expert answers. This chapter independently answers and verifies the topics without copying or reconstructing locked answers; difficulty and company labels are not treated as verified hiring statistics. 1. 13 Canonical Rules Must remember Characters are a UI quantity; tokens are a model-runtime quantity. A long context window is capacity; evidence utilization is empirical. Sampling controls variability; it does not create truth. Semantic similarity is candidate generation, not correctness. Syntax validity is not semantic validity, and semantic validity is not authorization. Capacity, selection, and reuse are separate design axes. ← Contents 02 Enterprise Retrieval Foundations →

textEn: CHAPTER 02 Enterprise Retrieval Foundations EXACT · BM25 · DENSE · GRAPH · METADATA W WHY W WHEN P PITFALL Five Common Retrieval Capabilities in Enterprise RAG They are not substitutes for one another; they solve different problems : identifiers, terminology, semantics, relationships, and scope. EXACT For structured fields / normalized strings, use deterministic matching . keyword field · term query · PK lookup · hash · alias. Suitable for order IDs · error codes · part numbers · VIN · SKU · API names · version numbers BM25 Inverted index, lexical relevance Ranking by term frequency, rarity, and document length. Suitable for domain terms · product names · error descriptions · technical / API / regulatory documents · function names DENSE Encode the Query and documents as embeddings, then use vector similarity to find semantically similar content. Suitable for natural-language Q&A · colloquial phrasing · synonyms · users unfamiliar with terminology · cross-language queries GRAPH Instead of searching for "which text looks most similar," traverse entity relationships to find the answer. Neo4j / SPARQL / Property Graph. Suitable for BOM · ERP/PLM · org structures · dependencies · multi-hop reasoning · impact analysis META It does not understand the answer itself; it is responsible for narrowing the search space first . Fields tenant · role · country · language · doc type · version · effective date · confidentiality level Capability Principle Strengths Limitations / Traps Exact Deterministic field matching Fast, stable, and explainable Does not understand paraphrases or synonyms; "exact" matching usually still requires normalization (E4307 / E-4307 / Error E 4307 → uppercase, remove spaces, normalize hyphens, alias mapping) BM25 Lexical matching + relevance ranking Fast, cheap, explainable, and sensitive to rare terms Does not understand semantics; "How can I get my money back?" vs "Refund and reimbursement policy" may have weak recall when lexical overlap is low; not a primary-key lookup Dense Embedding vector similarity Handles paraphrases and finds semantically similar content with different wording Unstable for identifiers / version numbers; cancel subscription and renew subscription are topically similar but semantically opposite in action ; changing the embedding model requires rebuilding the index Graph Entity-relation traversal Multi-hop and impact analysis: Supplier A → Material X → Product Y Requires entity/relation construction first; entity disambiguation and updates are costly Metadata Attribute filtering Reduces irrelevant recall, prevents stale-version contamination, isolates tenants, and improves latency/cost Overly strict relevance filters can hurt recall; tenant and ACL constraints must never be relaxed to improve recall FIG. 2. 1 Metadata filtering first: authorize before semantic retrieval STEP 1 User: What is the German refund policy for 2026? STEP 2 country = Germany valid_year = 2026 document_type = policy STEP 3 BM25 / Dense Retrieve only within the authorized candidate space STEP 4 Answer Must Remember ×3 Exact retrieval is best for identifiers, but it usually requires field-aware indexing and normalization. BM25 handles lexical relevance; it is strong for terminology but weaker for paraphrases. Dense retrieval handles meaning, but semantic similarity is not the same as factual or operational equivalence. Key Principle Authorization before semantic similarity. Unauthorized documents must not enter the model context. 2026-09-28 · Verification boundaries Exact normalization must preserve business identity, and ACLs cannot be relaxed for recall. It answers: What evidence does the current request need, which data path should be called, when should paths run in parallel, when should the system clarify, and when should it stop? Low-quality Answer "Run Exact, BM25, Dense, Graph, and the database every time, then choose the best." As a default for all requests, this ignores query-type differences, data-source boundaries, latency/cost budgets, permission risks, and recovery strategies. Reduce conversation into explicit topic, entity, and constraint state, then form the standalone retrieval query from relevant state. A topic switch invalidates topic-scoped working state, not every kind of memory. EVAL Do not evaluate only the final answer. Measure referent accuracy, standalone-query constraint recall, target-document Recall@K, topic-switch state leakage rate, and entity-mismatch rate so failures can be localized to state, rewrite, retrieval, or generation. Source note: this section engineering-reframes the user-provided summary on referential loss in multi-turn RAG. The source's claim that cost grows linearly with turns is retained as an implementation risk rather than a fixed cost law; the handbook additionally adds a failure taxonomy, evaluation slices, and the boundary with Chapter 07 working state and context compression.

textEn: CHAPTER 04 RAG Reliability and Selective Answering SIX GATES · RISK–COVERAGE G GATE F FAILURE M METRIC P PITFALL "100% Retrieval Accuracy" is nearly impossible to guarantee in an open enterprise knowledge base. A more realistic goal is 100% Trustworthy Answering : evidence available → answer; partially sufficient → partial answer; unclear → clarify; insufficient → retrieve more or refuse; high risk → escalate to a human. Why "refuse if you do not know" in the Prompt is not enough A Prompt can influence behavior, but it cannot prove that the Retriever missed nothing · the document truly supports the conclusion · documents do not conflict · no critical reasoning hop is missing · the document version is valid · the user is authorized. Prompt can encourage abstention. It cannot prove that abstention is correct. FIG. 4. 1 Six-layer Gate Pipeline STEP 1 Gate 0 · Query Analysis domain · intent · entity · time scope · risk · required evidence — "How much is it?" is missing an entity → Clarify instead of directly refusing as OOD STEP 2 Gate 1 · Knowledge Coverage supported domains · time coverage · entity catalog · document types · capability registry (theoretical coverage ≠ a concrete answer definitely exists) STEP 3 Gate 2 · Retrieval Quality Combined signals: Exact hit · Top-K score · Reranker score · Score margin · Retriever agreement · Source authority · Freshness · Metadata match. A low score only means "uncertain"; it does not prove "the knowledge base definitely has no answer." STEP 4 Gate 3 · Evidence Sufficiency Classification: SUPPORT / REFUTE / IRRELEVANT / INSUFFICIENT / CONFLICT. The question is not "is the document relevant?" but "is the evidence set sufficient to support the complete answer?" — Set-level checks: is a multi-hop link missing? do sources conflict? is there only background context? are some parts of a multipart question uncovered? STEP 5 Gate 4 · Claim Verification Answer → Claim Extraction → Claim–Evidence Alignment → Support Check. For every key Claim: evidence exists · citation is correct · scope is not exceeded · "possible" is not turned into "certain." STEP 6 Gate 5 · Decision Policy ANSWER · PARTIAL_ANSWER · CLARIFY · RETRIEVE_MORE · ROUTE_TO_OTHER_SOURCE · ESCALATE · REFUSE Must Remember Relevant evidence is not necessarily sufficient evidence. How to Set the Threshold G GATE M METRIC P PITFALL # ✗ Do not hard-code if similarity < 0. 8: refuse() FIG. 4. 2 Calibration Flow STEP 1 Representative Evaluation Set Answerable · Unanswerable in-domain · OOD · Outdated · Conflicting · Partial evidence STEP 2 Threshold Calibration Calibrate separately by domain / query type / language / retriever / risk Key Metrics and Trade-offs Coverage Selective Risk Unsafe Answer Rate False Refusal Rate Citation Correctness Citation Completeness Conflict Detection Rate Evidence Sufficiency Accuracy Risk–Coverage Curve More refusals reduce coverage, but selective risk falls only if the policy preferentially rejects wrong answers. Measure the risk–coverage curve , not a single accuracy point. High-quality Refusal Template I could not find sufficient evidence in the approved knowledge sources to answer this reliably. I found general information about the process, but not the specific threshold you asked about. Please provide the relevant policy version or ask an authorized expert to confirm it. Include: what was found · what is missing · why the system cannot answer · the next step. But must not reveal "there is a sensitive file you are not authorized to access." 2026-09-28 · Verification boundaries Coverage is answered requests divided by all requests. Selective risk is wrong answers divided by answered requests, undefined with zero answers. More refusals do not guarantee lower risk. Six Gates is an engineering synthesis, not proof of future reliability. Selective Classification ← 03 Hybrid Retrieval and Query Routing 05 Production-grade PDF RAG →

textZh: CHAPTER 05 生产级 PDF RAG P·R·I·T + C·E F FAILURE G GATE M METRIC “PDF → 抽文本 → 固定长度切分 → 向量库”在真实企业文档上会失败：目录多栏、页眉页脚、复杂表格、流程图、扫描页、盖章签名、跨页引用。结果是 阅读顺序错乱、表格行列丢失、标题正文割裂、页眉污染召回、图表信息消失 。生产级方案 = 四层处理 + 两条底线 。 FIG.5.1 总览：Parse → Reconstruct → Index → Tool ＋ Citation ＋ Evaluation STEP 1 ① Parse 解析 先识别文档 / 页面类型，再选择解析路径 STEP 2 ② Reconstruct 结构重建 恢复层级、阅读顺序与定位基因 STEP 3 ③ Index 语义切片 + 混合索引 按信息类型进入不同索引路径 STEP 4 ④ Tool Chain 受控文档工具 按需翻阅，而不是暴力通读 底线一 Page-level Citations + Claim Verification 关键论断绑定 document · page · section/table · excerpt。 底线二 分层评测闭环 评测要能回答“哪一层失败了”，而不只是“最终答案错了”。 第一层 · Parsing：先分类，再选解析路径 NATIVE 原生文本 PDF 直接读取 text span · font · bounding box · page coordinate · reading order candidate。 重点：保留位置和版式信息 ，为结构恢复提供依据。 SCAN 扫描件 PDF 本质是图片容器，需 OCR 输出：识别文本 · bbox · confidence · 页旋转 · 语言。低置信区域不能悄悄入库：重新识别 / 换模型 / 标低质量证据 / 人工复核。 MIXED 图文混排 PDF Layout parser + 图/图表抽取 + Vision-language 理解。输出不应只是“这是一张图”，而应形成可检索语义： “Figure 4 shows an approval workflow: request → manager review → finance review → payment release.” 核心原则 Choose the extraction method by document and page type; do not force every PDF through one parser. 第二层 · Structure Reconstruction：恢复文档语义 FIG.5.2 结构树 + 定位基因 Document ├── Chapter │ ├── Section │ │ ├── Paragraph │ │ ├── Table │ │ └── Figure │ └── Footnote └── Appendix 每个信息点携带“定位基因”： document_id · page · section_path paragraph_id · table_id · figure_id bounding_box 多栏阅读顺序： 按页面对象顺序抽取会出现“左栏一段 → 右栏一段”交错，必须恢复列、块与正确阅读顺序，并把标题层级附着到正文。 页眉页脚： 跨页重复模式识别后删除正文副本，或保留为专门 metadata，避免反复进入 Embedding。 表格： 恢复 row / column / header / merged cell / unit / caption / 跨页续表关系，存为 Markdown / CSV / JSON / DB 行，支持精确查询、范围过滤、数值比较、聚合。 图像： 绑定 figure number · caption · 周围段落 · page · section · vision 描述。 必背 Structure reconstruction turns page objects into traceable document semantics. 第三层 · Semantic Chunking 与 Hybrid Index CHUNK 结构感知切片规则 同一标题下连续段落 → 一个或多个语义 chunk · 完整条款尽量保持完整 · 完整表格单独结构化 · 图 + caption + 描述绑定为 figure chunk · 超长章节在子标题/段落边界继续切。 权衡： 过小 → 缺上下文、检索碎片化；过大 → 召回不精确、上下文成本高。 Contextual Enrichment 孤立 chunk “Revenue decreased by 12%.” → 补充短上下文（来自第 3 章 Currency Risk，描述 2025 财年汇率影响）。 原文与模型生成的上下文必须分开存储 ，避免把生成摘要误当原始证据。 信息类型 索引路径 自然语言段落 Dense + BM25 合同条款与术语 BM25 + Dense 编号、日期、版本 Exact / Keyword fields 结构化表格 SQL / 结构化存储 + lexical 章节、页码、权限 Metadata filter 跨实体关系 Optional graph index { "document_id" : "policy-2026-de" , "page" : 17 , "section_path" : [ "3 Risk Factors" , "3.2 Currency Risk" ], "content_type" : "paragraph" , "language" : "en" , "version" : "2026" , "valid_from" : "2026-01-01" , "access_scope" : "finance-eu" } 核心原则 Do not embed everything in the same way. Index according to the information type and the expected query operation. 第四层 · Agent Tool Chain：按需翻阅 FIG.5.3 受控工具执行过程 STEP 1 分析问题需要哪些证据 STEP 2 search_pdf(query, filters) STEP 3 read_page / read_section STEP 4 extract_table / analyze_chart STEP 5 quote_source(chunk_id) STEP 6 生成答案 → Claim Verification 好处： 上下文更小成本更低 · 工具调用可记录可重放 · 表格图表由专门工具处理 · 证据不足时可继续翻页 · 每步可定位失败原因。 约束： input schema · permission checks · maximum calls · allowed scope · timeout · logging · idempotency。 必背 The agent decides what evidence it needs; deterministic document tools control how that evidence is retrieved. 底线一 · Page-level Citations 与 Claim Verification FIG.5.4 引用校验流程 STEP 1 Draft answer STEP 2 Extract claims STEP 3 Match each claim to evidence STEP 4 Check entailment & scope STEP 5 Remove / qualify / refuse 无支持 claim 例：文档只说 “The policy may be reviewed annually.” ，系统不能扩写为 “The policy is updated every year.” 。 Citation correctness （引用是否真的支持 Claim）＋ Citation completeness （所有关键 Claim 是否都有引用）。合同、财报、风控、合规场景，缺页码和原文证据的答案不应视为完成。 底线二 · 分层评测闭环 层 指标 Parsing OCR Character / Word Error Rate · OCR confidence coverage · Reading-order accuracy · Page classification accuracy Structure Heading hierarchy accuracy · Table cell accuracy · Header/footer removal accuracy · Figure-caption association accuracy Retrieval Page Recall@K · Chunk Recall@K · Table Retrieval Recall · MRR / NDCG · Metadata-filter correctness Evidence & Answer Evidence sufficiency accuracy · Citation correctness / completeness · Answer correctness · False refusal rate · Unsafe answer rate FIG.5.5 错误诊断树：答案错误 → 失败在哪一层？ 正确页面没进索引 → Parsing / ingestion failure 页面存在但没被召回 → Retrieval failure 召回正确但表格解析错 → Structure / table failure 证据正确但结论超原文 → Generation / verification failure 证据不足仍回答 → Decision-policy failure 必背 A production evaluation should tell us which stage failed, not only that the final answer was wrong. 权限、版本与生命周期 Tenant isolation · Document-level ACL · Page/section 限制 · Version validity · Superseded 文档 · Retention/deletion · Index refresh · Audit trail。权限过滤尽量发生在 检索前 ，返回前再校验一次。版本冲突结合 valid_from/valid_to · supersedes · region · BU · source authority；仍无法确认有效版本 → 明确拒答或升级，而不是随机选一篇相关文档。 90 秒英文答案（见第 11 章 · 可复制） A production PDF RAG system is more than text extraction followed by embeddings. I would design it as a four-layer document-intelligence pipeline… Every important claim must be supported by a page-level citation. 完整版在 。 诚信映射 不应声称已完整上线生产级 PDF RAG。可说： “My direct experience is stronger in retrieval workflows, case-based reasoning, validation, fallback logic, structured artifacts, and tool-oriented agent systems. I understand how those principles extend to PDF RAG: parsing and structure recovery must be separated from retrieval, evidence must preserve provenance, and the agent should use controlled tools rather than treating the whole document as one prompt.” 2026-09-28 · 验证边界 OCR 字段支持依引擎而异；未知 confidence 不能伪造。Chunk 大小对 Recall 与 Precision 要分别评测。解析质量约束文本索引；重新读取原始页面/图像可以提供补救路径。原有 newsletter 实例全文本次未能取得。 PDF，并让本地 Ollama 模型完成检索与回答，同时返回精确页面引用；生产系统应在这个基础上继续补齐证据充分性判断、引用校验与拒答边界。 FIG.5.Y Grounded Document Agent = provenance-preserving retrieval + support gate + citation verification 解析质量决定检索上限；Grounding 质量取决于答案是否被原始证据真正支持，而不是页面上是否出现了一个 citation 字符串。 1 · PARSE 结构化解析，而不是只抽纯文本 尽量保留 page boundary、heading hierarchy、table、figure、reading order 与可定位的 layout metadata。 2 · INDEX Chunk 不能切断 provenance 每个 EvidenceChunk 至少携带 document_id、page、section、chunk_id 与 parser provenance；布局敏感任务再保留 bbox / element metadata。 3 · RETRIEVE 检索 Evidence Bundle，而不是孤立相似片段 查询可组合 semantic retrieval、keyword / metadata filter、reranking，并在需要时读取相邻页或同一 section 的连续上下文。 4 · SUPPORT GATE 先判断证据够不够，再决定是否回答 不足时应扩展检索、重写 query、检查相邻 section，或者直接 abstain；不要把“检索到了东西”误当成“足够支持答案”。 5 · ANSWER 只基于当前 Evidence Bundle 生成 回答中的关键 claim 应映射回一个或多个 source span，并携带 page / section citation。 6 · VERIFY 验证 claim ↔ evidence，而不是只验证 citation 存在 Citation Presence 只是第一层；更重要的是 Citation Correctness 与 Claim–Evidence Entailment。失败时修复回答、重新检索或拒答。 GROUNDING CONTRACT Citation Presence ≠ Citation Correctness。页面号存在，只能证明系统打印了引用；真正的可靠性要求引用页面支持对应 claim，并且用户能够回到原文验证。 PARSING CEILING Document QA quality ≈ Parsing × Retrieval × Evidence Selection × Generation × Citation Verification。解析阶段把表格、阅读顺序或页边界破坏之后，后面的 embedding 与 LLM 很难恢复原始语义。 EvidenceChunk：把 provenance 当成一等数据 Field 为什么需要 生产用途 document_id 区分来源与版本 权限、去重、更新与 lineage page / section 保留人类可验证的位置 页面引用、邻页扩展与 section-aware retrieval chunk_id 为证据建立稳定标识 缓存、评估、回放与错误分析 bbox / element 保留视觉文档的局部位置 表格、图像、highlight 与 multimodal verification parser_provenance 知道文本是如何被解析出来的 parser regression、版本比较与重建索引 retrieval_score 记录为何进入 Evidence Bundle threshold、reranking、eval 与 failure analysis AGENTIC BOUNDARY 普通 RAG 可以是一次 retrieve → generate；Agentic Document QA 的价值从“检索变成决策过程”开始：系统根据当前证据决定继续检索、扩大范围、查看相邻页面、重写查询或拒答。这个循环应保持 bounded，并把停止条件、最大检索轮数和权限边界写清楚。 FAIL 常见错误：把 citation 当装饰 只检查“有没有 [Page 17]”会放过错误引用。更可靠的评估单位是 claim：每个关键 claim 是否有匹配 evidence，evidence 是否真的蕴含该 claim。 GATE 正确边界：证据不足时允许不回答 Grounded system 的目标不是最大化 answer rate，而是最大化 supported answer rate。证据不足时 abstain，是可靠性机制，不是失败。 SOURCE / SCOPE 来源示例：AI Engineering 的 Hands-On: Build a Grounded Document Agent。公开项目说明确认了 long-PDF QA、LlamaParse、Ollama 与精确页面引用。上面的 support gate、claim–evidence verification、bounded re-retrieval 与 abstention 是本手册基于生产 RAG / Agent reliability 原则做的工程化扩展，而不是对原教程逐句复述。 AI Engineering source . 相关章节：证据不足时的选择性回答与拒答见 Chapter 04；bounded agent loop、停止条件与恢复边界见 Chapter 08。 Ch.04 · Ch.08
textEn: CHAPTER 05 Production-grade PDF RAG P·R·I·T + C·E F FAILURE G GATE M METRIC "PDF → extract text → fixed-length chunking → vector database" fails on real enterprise documents: multi-column tables of contents, headers/footers, complex tables, flowcharts, scanned pages, stamps/signatures, and cross-page references. The result is wrong reading order, lost table rows/columns, broken title–body structure, header/footer contamination in retrieval, and missing chart information . A production-grade solution = four processing layers + two hard requirements . FIG. 5. 1 Overview: Parse → Reconstruct → Index → Tool + Citation + Evaluation STEP 1 ① Parse First identify the document/page type, then choose the parsing path STEP 2 ② Reconstruct Structure Recover hierarchy, reading order, and positioning metadata STEP 3 ③ Index: Semantic Chunking + Hybrid Index Route different information types into different indexing paths STEP 4 ④ Tool Chain: Controlled Document Tools Read on demand instead of brute-force reading everything Hard Requirement 1 Page-level Citations + Claim Verification Bind key claims to document · page · section/table · excerpt. Hard Requirement 2 Layered Evaluation Loop Evaluation must answer "which layer failed," not merely "the final answer was wrong." Layer 1 · Parsing: Classify First, Then Choose the Parsing Path NATIVE Native-text PDF Directly extract text span · font · bounding box · page coordinate · reading-order candidates. Focus: preserve positional and layout information to support structure reconstruction. SCAN Scanned PDF Essentially an image container; OCR should output recognized text · bbox · confidence · page rotation · language. Low-confidence regions must not silently enter the index: re-recognize / switch models / mark as low-quality evidence / send for human review. MIXED Mixed text-and-image PDF Use a layout parser + image/chart extraction + vision-language understanding. The output should not merely say "this is an image"; it should produce retrievable semantics: "Figure 4 shows an approval workflow: request → manager review → finance review → payment release." Core Principle Choose the extraction method by document and page type; do not force every PDF through one parser. Layer 2 · Structure Reconstruction: Recover Document Semantics FIG. 5. 2 Structure Tree + Location Metadata Document ├── Chapter │ ├── Section │ │ ├── Paragraph │ │ ├── Table │ │ └── Figure │ └── Footnote └── Appendix Each information unit carries "location metadata": document_id · page · section_path paragraph_id · table_id · figure_id bounding_box Multi-column Reading Order: Extracting by raw page-object order can interleave "left-column paragraph → right-column paragraph." Recover columns, blocks, and correct reading order, and attach title hierarchy to body text. Headers and Footers: Detect repeated cross-page patterns and remove their body-text duplicates, or retain them only as dedicated metadata so they do not repeatedly enter embeddings. Tables: Recover row / column / header / merged cell / unit / caption / cross-page continuation relationships. Store as Markdown / CSV / JSON / DB rows to support exact queries, range filters, numerical comparisons, and aggregation. Images: Bind figure number · caption · surrounding paragraphs · page · section · vision description. Must Remember Structure reconstruction turns page objects into traceable document semantics. Layer 3 · Semantic Chunking and Hybrid Index CHUNK Structure-aware Chunking Rules Continuous paragraphs under the same heading → one or more semantic chunks · keep complete clauses together when possible · store complete tables separately in structured form · bind image + caption + description as a figure chunk · split very long sections again at subheading/paragraph boundaries. Trade-off: Too small → missing context and fragmented retrieval; too large → imprecise recall and higher context cost. Contextual Enrichment For an isolated chunk "Revenue decreased by 12%." → add a short context prefix (from Chapter 3 Currency Risk, describing the FX impact in fiscal year 2025). Store source text separately from model-generated context to avoid treating generated summaries as original evidence. Y The goal of long-document QA is not merely to find similar text, but to make every answer traceable through Evidence Chunk → Page / Section → Source Document. The public project example uses LlamaParse to parse long PDFs and local Ollama models for retrieval and answering while returning exact page citations; a production system should extend this with evidence-sufficiency checks, citation validation, and abstention boundaries. FIG. 5. Y Grounded Document Agent = provenance-preserving retrieval + support gate + citation verification Parsing quality sets the upper bound for retrieval. Grounding quality depends on whether the answer is actually supported by source evidence, not whether a citation string merely appears beside it. 1 · PARSE Parse structure, not just plain text Preserve page boundaries, heading hierarchy, tables, figures, reading order, and locatable layout metadata whenever possible. 2 · INDEX Chunking must preserve provenance Each EvidenceChunk should carry at least document_id, page, section, chunk_id, and parser provenance; layout-sensitive tasks should also keep bbox or element metadata. 3 · RETRIEVE Retrieve an evidence bundle, not isolated similar fragments A query may combine semantic retrieval, keyword or metadata filters, reranking, and neighboring-page or same-section context when continuity matters. 4 · SUPPORT GATE Judge evidence sufficiency before deciding to answer If support is insufficient, expand retrieval, rewrite the query, inspect neighboring sections, or abstain. Do not confuse 'something was retrieved' with 'the answer is supported.' 5 · ANSWER Generate only from the current evidence bundle Each material claim should map back to one or more source spans and carry page or section citations. 6 · VERIFY Verify claim ↔ evidence, not merely citation presence Citation Presence is only the first layer. More important are Citation Correctness and Claim–Evidence Entailment. On failure, repair the answer, retrieve again, or abstain. GROUNDING CONTRACT Citation Presence ≠ Citation Correctness. A page number only proves that the system printed a citation; reliability requires the cited source to support the corresponding claim and to remain inspectable by the user. PARSING CEILING Document QA quality ≈ Parsing × Retrieval × Evidence Selection × Generation × Citation Verification. Once parsing destroys table structure, reading order, or page boundaries, stronger embeddings and LLMs usually cannot reconstruct the original semantics reliably. EvidenceChunk: Treat provenance as first-class data Field Why it matters Production use document_id Distinguishes source and version Permissions, deduplication, updates, and lineage page / section Preserves a human-verifiable location Page citations, neighboring-page expansion, and section-aware retrieval chunk_id Creates a stable evidence identifier Caching, evaluation, replay, and error analysis bbox / element Preserves local position in visual documents Tables, figures, highlights, and multimodal verification parser_provenance Records how the text was produced Parser regression analysis, version comparison, and index rebuilds retrieval_score Records why the chunk entered the evidence bundle Thresholding, reranking, evals, and failure analysis AGENTIC BOUNDARY Ordinary RAG may be a single retrieve → generate pass. Agentic Document QA begins when retrieval becomes a decision process: the system uses current evidence to decide whether to retrieve again, widen scope, inspect neighboring pages, rewrite the query, or abstain. Keep this loop bounded, with explicit stopping conditions, retrieval limits, and permission boundaries. FAIL Common failure: treating citations as decoration Checking only whether '[Page 17]' exists will miss incorrect citations. A better evaluation unit is the claim: does every material claim have matching evidence, and does that evidence actually entail the claim? GATE Correct boundary: allow no-answer when evidence is insufficient A grounded system should not maximize answer rate; it should maximize supported answer rate. Abstaining when evidence is insufficient is a reliability mechanism, not a failure. SOURCE / SCOPE Source example: AI Engineering's Hands-On: Build a Grounded Document Agent. A This chapter is not only about selecting a Skill. A production system must separate capability contracts, control flow, protocol access, and real side-effect execution; otherwise Skill, MCP, function calling, and tools collapse into one ambiguous layer. FIG. 6. A1 · CAPABILITY ARCHITECTURE From business intent to real execution: a five-layer capability stack Upper layers decide what should be done; lower layers define how capability access is exposed and who actually executes it. Authorization and validation cross every boundary. LAYER 1 Business Goal / User Intent Goal, risk, current state, and user permissions determine which capability is needed. LAYER 2 Skill Contract / Capability Registry when_to_use · when_not_to_use · inputs/outputs · permission · risk · owner · version LAYER 3 Workflow / State Machine / Policy Gate Controls execution order, missing inputs, approvals, retries, stopping, and recovery. A Skill is not a raw tool call. LAYER 4 MCP / Function Calling / API Interface Provides capability exposure, schemas, discovery, transport, or structured action proposals; these are not the final business-authorization decision. LAYER 5 Host Execution → Tool / API / DB / Service The host performs schema validation, authorization, idempotency, timeouts, and logging, and owns real side effects. Boundary rule Protocol exposes capabilities; Skill defines reusable task procedure; Workflow controls execution; Host owns authority and side effects. Intent Routing: do not make one mechanism handle all traffic §6. B Production intent recognition is not a rules-versus-LLM choice. Escalate by confidence, task complexity, risk, and cost. Cheap deterministic requests should exit early; only ambiguous or compositional tasks should reach the expensive planner. FIG. 6. B1 · COST-AWARE ROUTING CASCADE From deterministic fast paths to a structured planner Every layer needs an uncertainty exit. Unresolved requests escalate instead of being forced into a label. INPUT User Turn + State Update current task, active entity, filled slots, corrections, and topic-scoped state first. FAST PATH Deterministic Gate Exact mapping · regex · FSM · typed command. Admit only stable, low-ambiguity, high-confidence boundaries. CONTEXT State-aware Router Referent resolution · continuation/topic shift · lightweight classifier / semantic match · confidence gate. ESCALATE Structured LLM Planner Handles ambiguous, compositional, and multi-step requests; emits typed capability/tool proposals rather than only guessing an intent label. CONTROL Permission · Risk · Input Gate → Host Capability matching is followed by authorization, schema checks, approvals, idempotency, and result validation. The host owns real execution authority. Escalation rule Escalate by uncertainty, task complexity, and risk—not by a fixed technology ladder. FIG. 6. B1A · ROUTING FUNNEL ECONOMICS As requests move down the funnel, traffic falls while ambiguity, complexity, and per-request cost rise The funnel is not about forcing a target traffic percentage. It lets simple, stable requests exit early and reserves expensive reasoning budget for the long tail that actually needs it. L1 · WIDE Deterministic Fast Path High-volume, low-ambiguity, low unit cost. Admit stable commands, regex/FSM, and typed actions without endlessly encoding edge cases into the rule set. L2 · CORE Context-aware Router Handles most routine semantic traffic. Quality depends on state freshness, referent resolution, continuation/topic-shift detection, and lightweight classification or semantic matching. L3 · NARROW Structured LLM Planner Low-volume, high-ambiguity, high unit cost. Use for cross-domain, compositional, multi-step, and dynamic-tool-choice requests, producing structured capability or tool proposals. Dimension L1 L2 L3 Traffic share high medium low Ambiguity low medium high Task complexity low medium high Unit latency / cost low medium high ANTI-PATTERN Rule Black Hole Every new edge case becomes another regex or exception, creating growing precedence, conflict, test-surface, and ownership debt. ANTI-PATTERN LLM Front Door Every request starts with the most expensive model, adding unnecessary latency, cost, and output variance while exposing deterministic problems to probabilistic behavior. Funnel rule Reduce average decision cost without hiding uncertainty or turning the fast path into a rule warehouse. FIG. 6. B2 · ROUTING DECISION BOUNDARIES Intent, capability, and authorization are three different decisions 1 Intent Understanding What is the user trying to achieve? Does this turn depend on prior state, entities, or slots? 2 Capability Routing Which Skill, Workflow, or Tool combination can satisfy the goal? Allow DIRECT, MULTI, CLARIFY, and NO_MATCH. 3 Authorization / Execution May this user invoke it now? Does risk require approval? Are arguments complete? Can the host execute safely? C Jev is better understood as a typed probabilistic decision layer, not a smaller chat model. It handles predefined Noul, Choice, and Score decisions; open generation, complex planning, and multi-step reasoning remain System-Two LLM work. FIG. 6. C1 · SYSTEM-ONE + SYSTEM-TWO Fast decisions handle closed judgments; deliberative reasoning handles open tasks This is not a model-generation replacement story; it assigns different task shapes to different execution layers. STATE User / Program State Natural language, structured business state, agent traces, or other inputs that require a decision. SYSTEM ONE Typed Probabilistic Decisions Noul · Choice · Score Returns predefined types, probabilities, and confidence for classify / route / score / gate decisions. GATE Confidence + Policy High-confidence, low-risk cases can branch directly; uncertain, incomplete, or high-risk cases go to clarify, review, or escalation. SYSTEM TWO General LLM Planner Open generation, compositional intents, multi-step planning, code, reports, and tasks whose answer space cannot be enumerated in advance. CONTROL Authorization · Validation · Host Regardless of which model makes the decision, real side effects remain controlled by permissions, schemas, approvals, validation, and the host. Architecture rule Closed decision → typed probabilistic fast path. Open reasoning → general planner. FIG. 6. C2 · DECISION PRIMITIVES Three primitives map to three programmable decision shapes Primitive Output Best fit Noul Probability of truth [0, 1]; policy thresholds determine yes/no risk gate · condition · escalation Choice distribution over a defined candidate set + confidence intent · route · capability / tool choice Score scale rating + level distribution + confidence quality · risk · priority · relevance Critical boundary Type-safe ≠ semantically correct. Staying inside the schema does not guarantee a correct business judgment; confidence calibration, fallback, slice-based evaluation, and high-risk human review are still required. TIERS 6 LAYERS GOVERNANCE CQRS ISOLATED 01 EPHEMERAL ① Session Metadata conversation_id · user_id · tenant_id · locale · current task · permissions Scope: single session / request Ephemeral context 02 SHORT-TERM ② Working Memory (may expire after the task) current plan · intermediate results · open questions · tool outputs May expire when the task ends Execution intermediate state 03 USER PROFILE ③ Structured Profile (stable preferences) language preference · role · approved tools · report format Stable preferences · explicitly maintained Static profile 04 EVENT LOG ④ Episodic Memory (what happened) user asked X · system did Y · result was Z · feedback ± What happened · interaction traceability Episodic event stream 05 KNOWLEDGE ⑤ Semantic Memory (stable facts) organization / project facts · definitions · policies Stable facts · knowledge graph Enterprise facts 06 SKILL / PATTERN ⑥ Procedural Memory (reusable procedures) how to perform task X · validated workflow · repair strategy Reusable procedures · solution patterns Procedural skills 💡 Architecture layering principle: Short-term memory (①/②) flows through memory/Redis with the session lifecycle; long-term memory (③/④/⑤/⑥) must never be freely written by the model and must pass through Write Pipeline(FIG. 7. 2) structured extraction, permission checks, deduplication, and version conflict resolution before persistence. LEDGER Append-only Represent normal corrections as new events, while still enforcing deletion, redaction, retention, and derived-cache invalidation. VIEWS Current View current user profile / current state, derived from the event log. POLICY Governance Policy What can be written, read, expired, or shared. Each Memory record has two times: Valid Time and Transaction Time. FIG. 7. 2 Write Pipeline (do not let the model write freely) STEP 1 Conversation / Event STEP 2 Candidate Extraction → Normalize → Deduplicate STEP 3 Conflict Check → Permission / Policy Check STEP 4 Store(source · confidence · owner · scope · validity · sensitivity · version)→ Update Views FIG. 7. 3 Read Pipeline (do not read everything every time) STEP 1 Current Query STEP 2 Query Classification → Access Filter STEP 3 Retrieve Relevant Memory STEP 4 Rank by Relevance + Recency + Quality → Assemble Context Multi-user and Permission Isolation tenant_id · user_id · resource ACL · memory scope. Unauthorized Memory: must not enter retrieval candidates, must not enter model context, and must not have its existence leaked in a refusal. Honest Positioning of AutodidactAgent AutodidactAgent mainly implements episodic and procedural memory through solved cases and reusable skills. It is not a general-purpose user-profile memory system. It is closer to Solved Case + Best Skill + Score + Provenance than to general-purpose long-term user memory. Short-term → Long-term Memory Promotion G GATE F FAILURE M METRIC FIG. 7. 4 Memory Promotion Pipeline STEP 1 Working State STEP 2 Candidate Extraction STEP 3 Importance + Stability STEP 4 Dedup + Conflict Check STEP 5 Long-term Store + Provenance Short-term memory should not automatically "become" long-term memory. Promote only information that is stable, reusable, user-authorized, and low-conflict; temporary tool outputs, unverified inferences, and sensitive information should not be promoted by default. X Whether "budget must not exceed 5000" should survive across sessions depends first on scope and durability: it may be a current-task constraint, a durable project constraint, or a stable user preference. Memory architecture is about promotion, scope, provenance, conflict, and retrieval policy—not merely storage. FIG. 7. X1 · CROSS-SESSION MEMORY GOVERNANCE Promote on write, route on read, preserve lineage on conflict A long-history summary is only a Context View. Durable constraints need structured scope, provenance, validity, and supersession. WRITE 01 Candidate Extraction Extract candidate memories from explicit user statements, tool observations, or model inferences, and label source_kind first. WRITE 02 Scope + Durability Gate Resolve task, thread, project, user, or tenant scope plus temporary, stable, or expiring durability. Only truly durable information enters long-term storage. STORE Durable Memory + Provenance Persist not only the value but also source, confidence, valid_from / valid_to, supersedes, sensitivity, and owner. READ Memory Route + Filters The current decision determines which memory class is needed, followed by scope, permission, validity, and relevance filtering—not one global vector search over all history. CONFLICT Authority + Supersession Explicit correction, scope specificity, source authority, valid time, and confidence determine the active value together; newer does not automatically mean more authoritative. Core rule Write selectively. Read selectively. Expire explicitly. Correct with lineage. FIG. 7. If information was never persisted, a new thread has nothing to recall. Enterprise Knowledge Context: enterprise knowledge is governed context §7. K Enterprise knowledge infrastructure is not about pushing more text into a vector store. It turns organizational concepts, rules, workflows, cases, and live facts into versioned, authorized, traceable agent context. FIG. 7. K1 · KNOWLEDGE CONTEXT LIFECYCLE Source → Organize → Process → Serve → Govern → Agent Context SOURCE Documents · workflows · rules · cases · data provenance · owner · raw version ORGANIZE / PROCESS classify · relate · index · structure Do not vectorize everything. Preserve hierarchy, relationships, scope, and structured facts. SERVE RAG · API · Structured Query · File Search Choose the serving path by data shape, freshness, permission, and failure semantics. GOVERN version · permission · validity · correction owner · expiry · supersede · lineage · usage feedback CONTEXT Explainable, verifiable, authorized task context The agent consumes governed evidence, not an untraceable pile of text. Core rule Enterprise knowledge is governed context, not merely retrieved text.

X Do not treat loops and graphs as two generations of competing technology. A loop is a local autonomous control pattern for an agent; a graph is an explicit topology for organizing work units, decision boundaries, and recovery paths. FIG. 8. X Make the single loop controllable first; split into a graph only when structural boundaries appear Start with the smallest controllable loop. Add graph-level control-flow complexity only when coordination complexity requires explicit topology. LOOP Local autonomy around one coherent goal Goal → Observe → Reason / Plan → Act → Verify → Stop or iterate. Best when context is shared, the permission boundary is unified, verification is clear, and the stopping condition is explicit. GRAPH Explicit coordination across structural boundaries Router → bounded work units → branch / join → checkpoint → validation → recovery. Best for parallel branches, different context or permission domains, auditable decision points, and independent recovery. START Bounded Agent Loop First make state, stopping conditions, verification, and failure recovery controllable. BOUNDARY A structural boundary appears parallelism · different permissions · different contexts · branch / join · checkpoint / resume · failure isolation · human approval SPLIT Split the boundary into explicit graph nodes and edges Add only the control-flow complexity needed to solve a real coordination problem. UPGRADE When to upgrade from a loop to a graph Look for structural signals, not trend vocabulary: parallel tracks; different context, memory, or permission domains; explicit branch / join; checkpoint / resume; failure isolation; auditable control points; and human approval boundaries for high-risk actions. NODE A graph node is not necessarily an agent loop A node can be a deterministic function, retrieval step, tool execution, policy gate, human approval, sub-workflow, or an agent loop. A graph defines topology; it does not require every node to be autonomous. INTERACTIVE · ARCHITECTURE EXPLORER Does your task actually need a graph? Select only the coordination boundaries that actually exist. The recommendation updates live and highlights the smallest sufficient architecture: a loop, a gated loop, or an outer graph. Structural signals Parallel branches are required Multiple work units can or must progress concurrently Context or memory must be isolated Different work units should not share the full context Different permission domains exist Tools, data, or actions must be separated by explicit boundaries Branch / Join Control flow must explicitly branch and later join Checkpoint / Resume Execution must persist and resume from intermediate state Failure Isolation Local failures need independent recovery instead of rerunning everything Human Approval High-risk actions require an explicit human approval boundary Reset Recommended architecture Bounded Agent Loop 0 structural signals LOCAL BOUNDED LOOP Goal → Plan → Act → Verify → Done ↺ If verification fails, iterate within an explicit budget and stopping condition OUTER EXPLICIT GRAPH Router → Work A Work B → Join → Checkpoint Policy Gate CANONICAL RULE Use the least control-flow complexity that still makes state, stopping conditions, permissions, and recovery explicit. PITFALL A graph does not repair a broken loop. If the loop itself has broken state handling, verification, stopping conditions, or tool policy, wrapping it in a graph only creates a more complex system with the same underlying failure. LANGGRAPH State → Node → Patch → Route → Checkpoint Makes execution state and transitions explicit so branches, loops, retries, interrupt/resume, and HITL become inspectable control flow. FIG. 8. Use it to avoid rebuilding common capabilities. Coding Agent Engineering: From writing code to specifying, directing, and verifying §8. 7 Coding agents do not remove the software-engineering workflow; they redistribute engineering attention. Less time is spent typing code, while more time moves to deciding what to build, designing the architecture, writing a clear spec, calibrating agent autonomy, verifying results, and feeding later evidence back into earlier stages. They can also perform non-code execution such as data analysis and system operations, so the engineering problem is to govern the whole execution loop rather than code generation alone. FIG. 8. 7 The coding-agent workflow is still software engineering; what changes is who executes and where human attention goes Planning → Execution → Deployment & Monitoring is not a one-way pipeline. When verification or monitoring fails, return to an earlier stage to revise the spec, architecture, context, or execution plan. 1 · PLAN Research, understand the codebase, write the spec, decompose the plan Clarify requirements, technical design, architecture, constraints, and acceptance criteria before execution. Then interrogate assumptions, security risks, and overengineering. A greenfield prototype may need a light spec; a complex brownfield system needs much more rigorous planning and validation. 2 · EXECUTE Build, test, verify, and calibrate autonomy Decide which steps need tight human-agent iteration and which can be delegated as larger work units. At the same time, manage context, permissions, parallel agents, and the finite budget of human attention. 3 · DEPLOY / OBSERVE Deploy through gates, then use evidence to drive the next iteration Deploy through CI/CD and human gates where appropriate. Agents can watch logs, surface issues, and propose fixes, but high-risk side effects still need explicit permission, verification, and rollback boundaries. ITERATIVE, NOT LINEAR A verification failure is not merely a signal to regenerate code. It may reveal an unclear spec, a wrong architecture assumption, stale context, poor task decomposition, or an inadequate verifier. Problems found in monitoring may likewise require returning to planning rather than patching production locally. Five core skills: engineering judgment is the scarce resource Skill What the engineer actually decides Typical failure when weak Directing the workflow How deeply to plan, when to start executing or step back, when to retain human ownership, how to choose the architecture and write planning artifacts or specs, and how to trade off speed, cost, technical risk, and human effort. The agent quickly completes the wrong problem or keeps drifting without concrete acceptance criteria. Enabling agent autonomy How much autonomy each stage deserves; when to stay interactive, when to delegate a larger work unit or bounded loop, when to run agents in parallel, and how to manage context, permissions, gates, and blast radius. Long autonomous runs are mistaken for maturity, so mistakes spread faster, context drifts, or high-risk actions escape control. Reviewing the work What evidence proves completion: automated tests, behavioral and functional checks, screenshots or artifacts, eval sets, LLM-as-judge, agentic code review, security and architecture audits, and which critical points still require human judgment. The agent's own claim of completion is accepted as proof, or tests validate implementation details without validating the real objective. Customizing the agent and its environment How to provide tools and standing context with skills, plugins, MCP, hooks, and project-level instruction files; how to preserve necessary state across sessions, capture retrospectives, and prune obsolete capabilities and agent-generated debt. Every session starts from scratch, the agent repeatedly loses project context, tool permissions are too broad, or stale skills conflict with newer model capabilities. Coding agent foundations Understand how the agent searches code, retrieves context, uses its context window, calls tools and subagents, and how the harness constrains model behavior and context cost. You cannot diagnose why the agent overengineers, misses constraints, stops too early, or keeps executing confidently with the wrong context. AUTONOMY Autonomy is a stage-level control variable, not a maturity badge High autonomy fits work that is verifiable, reversible, and low-blast-radius. High-risk planning, permission changes, production side effects, and irreversible actions should retain stronger human gates. CONTEXT Context is engineering infrastructure, not a one-off prompt Project constraints, architecture assumptions, code style, data-access patterns, and the current spec need stable, maintainable carriers. When requirements change mid-project, update the context the agent actually reads rather than changing only the human mental model. CANONICAL RULE A coding agent is not an autonomous coder; it is an execution component inside a human-directed, testable, permissioned engineering loop. Verification is part of execution itself, not post-processing added after the work is supposedly complete. CANONICAL RULE Coding agents lower the cost of implementation; they raise the value of specification, verification, and engineering judgment. PITFALL Long-running autonomy is not a quality metric. What matters is whether the goal is clear, the context is correct, permissions are bounded, verification is trustworthy, and the engineer knows when to intervene, step back, or stop. CH08 → CH09 · CONTROL PLANE Chapter 08 owns Coding Agent build and execution: planning, delegation, tools, state, autonomy, and recovery. Chapter 09 provides the outer reliability control plane: validation, evals, observability, release gates, monitoring, and production evidence feedback. Reviewing the work therefore should not stop at local code review; it extends into post-release regression protection.
